description: ISP wireless device catalog with real-world specs, drawn from a mix of vendor datasheets, product pages, and FCC filings with varying verification depth. Per-field verification status is tracked in each device's `evidence` block (status legend: V, V(2nd), derived, UNVERIFIED, low-confidence).

devices.name: Ubiquiti airFiber 60
devices.notes: 60 GHz mmWave PTP. Requires clear LOS. Best for last-mile aggregation < 2 km.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Official FCC-filed manual says 1800 Mbps, NOT 1700 — catalog value not corrected.

max_range_km.note: Manual says '2+ km' — matches catalog's 2 as a rounded figure.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: 60 GHz radio gain matches (38 dBi), but this device also has a 5 GHz backup radio at 11 dBi gain that the catalog's single-radio model omits entirely.

tx_power_dbm.note: Manual says 25 dBm max conducted TX power (5/60 GHz combined), NOT 27 — catalog value not corrected.

frequency_ghz.note: Device is dual-radio: 60 GHz AND 5 GHz (U-NII) backup. Catalog's single `frequency_ghz:60` field cannot represent this — the 5 GHz backup radio is missing from the model entirely, not just imprecise.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Not published in the official manual.

standard.note: Manual doesn't mention 802.11ad — OS is 'airOS GP', protocol proprietary.

devices.name: Ubiquiti airFiber 60 LR
devices.notes: Extended-range version of airFiber 60 with higher gain antenna.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Current official datasheet says 1950 Mbps, NOT 1700 — catalog value has not been corrected; this entry flags the mismatch, not a confirmation.

max_range_km.note: Current official datasheet says 12+ km, NOT 3.5 km — large discrepancy, catalog value not corrected.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Older FCC-filed manual says 38 dBi, NOT 43 — current datasheet doesn't publish this figure at all.

tx_power_dbm.note: Not found in the current official datasheet or the older FCC manual — catalog's 27 dBm is not backed by any source found.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Same as tx_power_dbm — not published by the vendor for this UISP-era model.

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes a 57-71 GHz band, not a single figure — catalog's 60 is a loose simplification.

standard.note: Neither official document mentions 802.11ad — vendor calls the radio proprietary 'Wave Technology' under airOS.

devices.name: Ubiquiti LiteBeam 5AC Gen2
devices.notes: Low-cost CPE for WISP subscribers. airMAX AC protocol.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Vendor page says '450+ Mbps' — matches catalog.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Datasheet and techspecs page agree: 23 dBi — matches catalog.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet says 25 dBm output power, NOT 23 — catalog value not corrected.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Datasheet gives a per-modulation table from -96 dBm (best, BPSK 1/2) to -65 dBm (worst, 256QAM 5/6) — no single published figure. Catalog's -95 is close to the best-case end but not a value the vendor states directly.

max_range_km.note: Vendor does not publish a maximum range figure anywhere (confirmed absent from both the datasheet PDF and the techspecs page).

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes a 5150-5875 MHz band, not a single figure — catalog's 5.8 is a loose simplification.

standard.note: Datasheet calls it 'airMAX ac Protocol' (proprietary TDMA over 802.11ac PHY), not '802.11ac Wave 2' verbatim — plausible characterization, not the vendor's own term.

devices.name: Ubiquiti PowerBeam 5AC 400
devices.notes: Dual-feed dish for point-to-point links. Compact form factor.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet (PBE-5AC-400 row): 25 dBm output power — matches catalog.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Per-modulation table row '2x QPSK (1/2)' is literally -95 dBm — matches catalog (not the best-case figure, but a value printed verbatim in the table).

max_throughput_mbps.note: Datasheet: 'up to 450+ Mbps real TCP/IP throughput' (family-wide claim) — matches catalog.

max_range_km.note: No range figure (km or miles) anywhere in the 11-page datasheet.

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes 5150-5875 MHz worldwide band — catalog's 5.8 is a loose simplification.

standard.note: Datasheet calls it 'airMAX ac' (proprietary), not '802.11ac Wave 2' verbatim.

devices.name: MikroTik SXTsq 5
devices.notes: Budget PTMP CPE. RouterOS based. Good for dense subscriber deployments.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Official product page: 16 dBi — matches catalog.

tx_power_dbm.note: Product page: 28 dBm max (at 6 Mbit/s / MCS0), NOT 23 — catalog value not corrected.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Product page: -96 dBm best-case, catalog says -94 — 2 dB off from the best-case point, minor mismatch.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Vendor's own MEASURED bridging throughput (1518-byte, fast path) is 98.4 Mbps — same pattern as mikrotik-lhg5: catalog's 300 is roughly 3x the vendor's measured figure.

standard.note: Product page says '802.11a/n' — catalog drops the 802.11a mode.

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes a 5 GHz band, not a single figure.

max_range_km.note: Not listed on the official product page. Product is also marked 'Discontinued' by the vendor (no lifecycle field exists in this catalog schema).

max_throughput_mbps.note: Vendor's own MEASURED bridging throughput (1518-byte packets) is 98.4 Mbps — catalog claims 300, roughly 3x higher than the vendor's measured figure.

standard.note: Product page says '802.11a/n' — catalog drops the 802.11a mode, minor but not strictly correct.

devices.name: Cambium ePMP 1000
devices.notes: GPS-synchronized TDD PTMP base station. Reduces co-channel interference in dense deployments.

model.note: Catalog's model 'C050900C001A' does NOT appear among the 5 official sales model numbers for the ePMP 1000 GPS Sync Radio family (C050900A011A / C050900A112A / C050900A013A / C050900A211A / C050900P011A), nor in a separate web search for the exact string. Could be a typo, an older/unindexed revision, or fabricated — not resolved.

tx_power_dbm.note: Spec sheet gives a range (-17 to +30 dBm combined, to regional EIRP limit). Catalog's 27 falls inside that range but is not a published single figure.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Spec sheet gives -93 dBm (MCS0, 20 MHz) down to -69 dBm (MCS15) — catalog's -94 is close to but not an exact match for any published row.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Spec sheet: 'more than 200 Mbps of real user throughput' — consistent with catalog's 200 (vendor says '>200', catalog states it as an exact figure).

standard.note: Spec sheet explicitly says 'Cambium Proprietary' MAC layer, NOT 802.11n — catalog's standard label does not match.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: This radio is sold without an integrated antenna (paired with an external sector) — 0 is a reasonable convention for a 'radio-only' SKU, not verified against a specific published figure.

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes a 4910-5970 MHz band, not a single figure.

max_range_km.note: Not listed in the spec sheet.

devices.name: Cambium PMP 450m
devices.notes: Massive MIMO 16x2 AP. Highest capacity Cambium PMP platform. Up to 2 Gbps aggregate.

rx_sensitivity_dbm.note: Datasheet: 'Ultimate Sensitivity: -94 dBm' — matches catalog exactly.

max_throughput_mbps.note: Vendor's own highest published claim is 'more than 1.2 Gbps in a 40 MHz channel' — catalog's 2000 Mbps EXCEEDS the vendor's own stated maximum (1200).

max_range_km.note: Datasheet: 'Maximum Deployment Range: Up to 64 km (40 miles)'. Catalog's 40 looks like it was taken from the miles column and mislabeled as km — a suspected unit-confusion bug, not corrected here.

standard.note: Datasheet: MAC 'Cambium Networks proprietary', PHY '14x14 Multi-User MIMO OFDM' — catalog's 'Proprietary MU-MIMO' label is the most accurate of any SKU in this audit.

tx_power_dbm.note: Datasheet states Maximum EIRP +45 dBm for the integrated 90-degree sector antenna — catalog's tx_power_dbm:30 + antenna_gain_dbi:0 (implying ~30 dBm EIRP) is architecturally inconsistent with this being a sectorized AP, not a bare radio; ~15 dB short of the published EIRP.

antenna_gain_dbi.note: Same inconsistency as tx_power_dbm above — this SKU has an integrated sector antenna, so gain 0 doesn't fit the product architecture.

frequency_ghz.note: Vendor publishes a 5150-5925 MHz band. Also note: this datasheet verifies the 5 GHz variant (14x14 MIMO); Cambium also sells a 3 GHz PMP 450m variant (8x8 MIMO, per registry.md B07) with different specs — catalog's generic id doesn't state which band, so this evidence may not apply if the SKU is meant to represent the 3 GHz variant.
